proposals.lexicon_quote: Amphibious Combat Vehicle Family of Vehicles
proposals.rationale: The announcement names Amphibious Combat Vehicles (ACV) verbatim and the action is the exercise of options for 27 full-rate-production personnel variants and 17 command variants with fielding and support - vehicle production, which belongs to the Procurement, Marine Corps line 'Amphibious Combat Vehicle Family of Vehicles' (BLI 2025, doc 339) whose index row is 'The Amphibious Combat Vehicle (ACV)'. The only other ACV owner in the index is 0605611M, the RDT&E system development and demonstration PE, which is not where full-rate production vehicles are bought, so the procurement/development split resolves lens B's collision test cleanly. MARCORSYSCOM contract number (M67854) matches the Marine Corps line.

refute_a.reason: Firm-fixed-price exercise of options for 27 full-rate-production ACV personnel variants and 17 command variants with fielding and support — vehicle procurement against the Procurement, Marine Corps line that buys the ACV family; the vehicle is the program the line funds and 2025 carries only ACV names, so neither the platform test nor the rollup test bites.

refute_b.reason: 'The Amphibious Combat Vehicle (ACV)' is a verbatim collision with 0605611M, but that line is System Development and Demonstration by its own title and cannot be the home of the full-rate-production personnel and command variants this option exercise buys, so the rival does not link equally well.

proposals.announcement_evidence: the production of Aegis Weapon System AN/SPY-1D(V) Radar Transmitter Group, Missile Fire Control System MK 99 equipment, and associated engineering services
proposals.rationale: 'Aegis Weapon System' matches the index row 'AEGIS Weapon System (AWS)' on BLI 5231 (Ship Missile Support Equipment) almost exactly, but the evidence does not establish that this award executes that line's work: the announcement states the contract combines purchases for the Navy at only 17 percent against the Republic of Korea at 50 percent and Japan at 33 percent under Foreign Military Sales, so five-sixths of the production is foreign-funded, and the same AWS name is also owned by 0604307N (Surface Combatant Combat System Engineering). With the Navy share a minority and the owning line contested inside the index, the attribution claim - that this action paid for BLI 5231's own work - is not supported to the standard §1 sets. Recorded rather than dropped so the denominator shows the name was read and rejected on evidence.

proposals.announcement_evidence: the Strategic Weapon System Fire Control Subsystem development, production, sustainment, modernization, repair, installation, training and technical engin
proposals.rationale: The announcement names the Strategic Weapon System, which matches the index row 'Strategic Weapons System (SWS)' on BLI 5358 'Strategic Missile Systems Equip'. Two things keep it below the bar. First, the identical name is also owned by BLI 1045 (COLUMBIA Class Submarine), so the index itself does not say which line owns a fire-control award covering the US SSBN, UK SSBN and SSGN fleets. Second, the scope deliberately spans development, production, sustainment, modernization, repair, installation and training in one contract, which is the mixed-appropriation shape that the 2026-09-04 held-out study found breaking three of six refutations - there is no way to say from the paragraph that procurement money on this OPN equipment line is what paid for it. Weak, not wrong: the name is real and the line is plausible, the evidence is simply not decisive.

proposals.announcement_evidence: Strategic Weapon System Trident Fleet support, Trident II Shipboard Integration Increment 8, and navigation subsystem development efforts
proposals.rationale: Unlike records 1, 3 and 20, this Trident II action is not missile procurement: it is fleet support, shipboard integration and navigation subsystem development, and the record's own funding sentence begins 'Fiscal 2023 operat...' - operations money. Attaching an O&M-funded fleet-support and integration action to the Weapons Procurement 'Trident II Mods' line (BLI 1250, doc 342) is precisely the appropriation failure mode lens A exists to catch, so the Trident II name being present is not enough. The shipboard-integration content would sit more naturally on a shipboard systems line (5358 carries 'Shipboard System Integration (SSI)'), but the paragraph does not give enough to make that call either. Weak.

proposals.announcement_evidence: to exercise options for Air and Missile Defense Radar low-rate initial production
proposals.lexicon_quote: Air and Missile Defense Radar (AMDR) System
proposals.rationale: AMDR is AN/SPY-6, so the index row 'AN/SPY-6' on PE 0604522N is the right identity, but the money says this award is not that PE's work: the record states fiscal 2017 and 2016 SHIPBUILDING AND CONVERSION (Navy) funding of $327,146,998 is obligated at award, and 0604522N is an RDT&E line. LRIP radar units bought with SCN belong to the ship line that installs them, not to the radar development PE - the O&M-or-procurement-money-on-an-RDT&E-line pattern lens A hunts. Record 74 is a later option exercise on this same contract N00024-14-C-5315 with the same SCN funding and would duplicate (piid, pe_bli), so it is folded into this one weak rather than proposed again.

proposals.announcement_evidence: the production and delivery of 20 F135-PW-100 propulsion systems for the Navy, six F135-PW-100 propulsion systems for the Air Force
proposals.rationale: The only F135 name this org's index carries is 'F135 Engine Core Upgrade (ECU)' under PE 0604840N/0604840M, 'F-35 C2D2' - an RDT&E continuous-capability-development line for a specific engine upgrade. This award delivers production F135-PW-100 propulsion systems on an option exercise; production engines are bought on the F-35 aircraft procurement lines, not on the C2D2 development PE, and the ECU is a different effort from the engines being delivered here. Name present, attribution unsupported. Record 10 is another modification on this same contract N00019-18-C-1021 (initial spare F135 propulsion systems for the Global Spares Pool) and would duplicate (piid, pe_bli); it fails for the same reason and is folded in here.

proposals.announcement_evidence: additional United Kingdom (UK) Strategic Weapon Support System kit manufacturing, and submarine industrial base development and expansion
proposals.rationale: The announcement names 'Strategic Weapon Support System' kit, which lines up with the index row 'SSBN Strategic Weapon Support Systems (SWSS)' on BLI 0950 'Strategic Platform Support Equip'. But the kits named are explicitly UNITED KINGDOM kits, and the remainder of the scope is submarine industrial base development and expansion under the Integrated Enterprise Plan, which the paragraph says supports Columbia-class AND the Virginia-class and Ford-class nuclear shipbuilding enterprise. A foreign-kit plus three-class industrial-base action cannot be attributed to one US support-equipment line on this evidence. (The Columbia line's own 'Maritime Industrial Base (MIB)' row would be the other candidate, but record 64 already occupies (N0002417C2117, 1045) and the industrial-base money is not confined to Columbia.) Weak.

proposals.announcement_evidence: the procurement of 75 Lot 14 F/A-18E/F F414-GE-400 engines and associated devices for U.S. Navy (48 install)
proposals.rationale: The index has no F414 row at all; the nearest candidate is the airframe name 'FA-18E/F' on BLI 0145, doc 330, 'F/A-18E/F (Fighter) Hornet'. Install engines for a Lot buy are plausibly funded on the aircraft line, so this is not an outright §3 platform rejection, but the paragraph never names a program - it names an engine model and an airframe - and a third of the buy (24 install plus three spares) is for the government of Australia. Compounding it, BLI 0145 carries rows from two different documents (the bomb/fuze rows are doc 338 while this row is doc 330), which is exactly the shared-code situation the rubric warns can leave the loader unable to resolve which member is meant. Not linked.

proposals.announcement_evidence: delivery of 108 conventional takeoff and landing F135 propulsion systems, 27 short takeoff and vertical landing F135 propulsion systems
proposals.rationale: Same defect as record 28 on a different PIID: a Lot 19 long-lead and production delivery of 148 F135 propulsion systems across CTOL, STOVL and Carrier Variant, matched only against the index's 'F135 Engine Core Upgrade (ECU)' row on the F-35 C2D2 RDT&E PE. Production propulsion systems and global spares are not the Engine Core Upgrade, and a production delivery order does not execute a continuous-capability-development line. The F135 name is present, the attribution is not supported.

proposals.announcement_evidence: U.S. and United Kingdom Trident II (D-5) Fleet Ballistic Missile Submarines Fire Control System
proposals.rationale: The paragraph names Trident II (D-5) but the deliverable is the SSBN Fire Control System, the SSGN Attack Weapon Control System and Support Equipment Rework Facility support - fire-control and support-equipment work, not missile production, so the Trident II name here points at the platform's weapon system rather than at the 'Trident II Mods' missile line. The nearest true owner is 'Strategic Weapons System (SWS)' on BLI 5358 'Strategic Missile Systems Equip', but that same name is also owned by BLI 1045 (COLUMBIA Class Submarine) and the announcement mixes US and UK scope across four fiscal years, so neither the owner nor the money colour is settled by the evidence. Weak.

proposals.announcement_evidence: procure F-135 propulsion system spare parts and depot lay-in material
proposals.rationale: Third F135 record, third distinct PIID, same failure: the award is an IDIQ ceiling increase for F-135 propulsion system SPARE PARTS and depot lay-in material serving Air Force, Marine Corps, Navy, FMS customers and non-DoD participants, matched only against the index's 'F135 Engine Core Upgrade (ECU)' row on the F-35 C2D2 RDT&E PE. Spares and depot lay-in are sustainment, the ECU is a development effort, and the customer mix is service-wide - nothing here says this action executed 0604840N's own work.

proposals.announcement_evidence: the procurement of eight F414-GE-400 install engines for the Navy
proposals.rationale: Weaker than record 32 on the same reasoning: eight install engines are for the Navy while 56 install engines, four spare engines, two containers and twelve spare modules are for the government of Kuwait, so the award is overwhelmingly Foreign Military Sales. The airframe name 'FA-18E/F' (BLI 0145, doc 330) is the only candidate the index offers - there is no F414 row - and an FMS-dominated engine buy does not establish that the Navy aircraft line's own work was paid for. Not linked.

proposals.announcement_evidence: Strategic Weapons Systems Fire Control Subsystem production to support the Common Missile Compartment production requirement
proposals.rationale: The Common Missile Compartment is named, and 0603595N is its only owner in the index, but the award's deliverable is Strategic Weapons System Fire Control Subsystem PRODUCTION that supports the CMC production requirement - so CMC is the thing being supported, one step removed from the work being bought, and the paragraph also flags a UK foreign military sale. Production support on an RDT&E development PE is the appropriation shape lens A breaks proposals on. Record 60, where the contract's own scope is CMC development and launcher hardware, is the version of this program that meets the standard; this one does not.

proposals.announcement_evidence: the procurement of 231 Tomahawk Block IV All-Up-Round missiles for the U.S. Navy
proposals.rationale: This is a NEW all-up-round buy - 231 missiles in vertical launch, capsule launch and UK torpedo-tube configurations - not the modification work BLI 2301 'Tomahawk Mods' funds. The missile identity is right (UGM-109E is Tomahawk Block IV) but the Tomahawk production line that would own a new-build procurement is not in this org's index at all, so there is no correct row to link and forcing it onto the Mods line would publish the wrong claim. Contrast record 53, a recertification and modernization action, which does belong on the Mods line. Weak by design rather than linked to the nearest available code.

proposals.announcement_evidence: support to execute in-service engineering agent (ISEA) functions for afloat and ashore tactical networks (TACNET)
proposals.rationale: §3 generic services. The award is an IDIQ for in-service engineering agent functions - technical and engineering assistance, design analysis, accreditation, installation, integration, sustainment and life cycle support - for afloat and ashore tactical networks and C4I systems generally, with no program element named. 'Tactical networks (TACNET)' is a category, not the index's 'Battle Force Tactical Network' line (BLI 2437), and the paragraph's own words say the sustainment covers 'fielded systems through end-of-life replacement' across NIWC Pacific's portfolio. Engineering support services of exactly the kind §3 rejects by design; no refute pass should be spent on it.

proposals.announcement_evidence: the procurement of AN/ARC-210(v) radios for installation in over 400 strategic and tactical airborne, seaborne and land based (mobile and fixed) platforms
proposals.rationale: §3 platform/component inversion. The index's only ARC-210 rows ('ARC-210' and 'ARC-210 Radio Communication System (RCS)') sit on BLI 4269, 'UMCS-Unman Carrier Aviation (UCA) Mission Cntrl' - the MQ-25 mission-control line that BUYS ARC-210 radios as a component. This award is the service-wide radio production buy: radios for installation in over 400 airborne, seaborne and land platforms for the Navy, Marine Corps, Army, Coast Guard, other agencies and FMS customers. The named thing is a component another program consumes, not the program BLI 4269 funds, so linking it would assert that a fleet-wide radio buy executed the unmanned carrier aviation mission-control line. Records 48 and 52 are further modifications on this same contract N00421-18-D-0004 and are folded into this one rejection.

proposals.announcement_evidence: to procure an additional 8,490 AN/ARC-210(v) radios, and associated ancillary equipment and support
proposals.rationale: Same §3 rejection as record 33 on the successor contract (N0042123D0001): 8,490 AN/ARC-210(v) radios plus ancillary equipment for installation in over 400 platforms across the Navy, Marine Corps, Army, Coast Guard, other DoD agencies and FMS customers. The index's ARC-210 rows belong to BLI 4269, the unmanned carrier aviation mission-control line that merely installs the radio; the radio is the component, that line is not the program this award funds. Record 58 is a further option exercise on this same PIID and is folded in here.

proposals.announcement_evidence: the procurement of 618 Joint Standoff Weapon (JSOW) air-to-ground missiles (AGM-154 Block III C)
proposals.rationale: §3 catch-all line, and doubly rejected on funding. The only JSOW row in this org's index is on BLI 6120 whose program title is 'Spares and Repair Parts' - an aggregate rollup, not a program, so a link asserting this award executed 'Spares and Repair Parts' is content-free in the same way the rubric's 'Items Less Than $5 Million' example is. Separately, the entire buy - 618 AGM-154 Block III C missiles, containers, spares and engineering technical assistance - is for the government of Saudi Arabia under Foreign Military Sales, so it is not a US line's own work in any case. Rejected without spending a refute pass.

proposals.announcement_evidence: logistics services in support of the C-12 utility lift aircraft, including post-production, full commercial-type aircraft maintenance, logistics support
proposals.rationale: §3 generic services - the award is contractor logistics support: post-production commercial-type aircraft maintenance, logistics support and materials for Marine Corps Reserve C-12 and Navy TC-12B aircraft across a dozen sites. Sustainment services against an aircraft procurement line is the exact appropriation error §3 and lens A reject, and the aircraft name (UC-12 on BLI 0562, 'Cargo/Transport A/C Series') is the PLATFORM the services support, not the program the line funds. Note the other UC-12 row, 'UC-12W' on BLI 0465, sits under 'Other Support Aircraft', which the loader's CATCHALL_TITLE pattern excludes outright, so neither candidate could publish.

proposals.announcement_evidence: combat system capabilities selection for international partner Canadian Royal Navy ships operating AEGIS
proposals.rationale: §3 platform, plus an unambiguous funding refutation stated in the record itself: 'Foreign Military Sales (Canada) (100%) funds in the amount of $126,174,827 will be obligated at time of award'. The work is modernization and new combat system capability selection for Canadian ships; AEGIS appears only as the system those foreign ships operate, not as the US program element being executed. A 100% FMS award cannot have paid for PE 0604307N's own work, so no link is possible regardless of which AEGIS row is chosen. (Record 42, the Australia Surface Combatant award on the same pattern, names no index program at all and gets no proposal.)

proposals.announcement_evidence: the modernization and upgrade of four P-3B aircraft in support of structural mid-life upgrades
proposals.rationale: The name matches the index row 'P-3 Modernization Program' (PE 0604221N) almost word for word, which is exactly why it needs rejecting rather than linking: the announcement says the work is a country-specific mission integration and management system, avionics and mid-life upgrade of four P-3B aircraft 'in support of the government of Greece', with 25 percent of the work in Schimatari and more in Argyroupoli. This is a foreign military sale modernizing Greek aircraft, not the US Navy P-3 Modernization PE's own work, so the surface name match is the trap. Rejected.
